extracted.intended_audience: educated general readers and natural philosophers interested in microscopy, particle theory, and natural theology (17th–18th century)
extracted.subtask_description: A didactic natural-philosophy essay arguing for the extreme smallness and vast number of particles (in water, air, light, solids) using microscopy observations, proportional calculations, and conservative estimates to persuade a general audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground claims on empirical observations (Leuwenhoek)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay down for a foundation the Experiments of Mr. Leuwenhoek, as they are described ... where he relates, that he distinguished in Pepper-Water, in the Sperm of Animals, &c. three sorts of Animalcula of different Sizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct microscopic observations (examples: pepper-water, sperm) as the empirical basis for estimates of particle sizes and counts; treat those observations as the starting point for numerical extrapolation.

rubrics_metrics.name: State assumptions explicitly for calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: Now to form a rough Conception ... let a Drop of Water be supposed to be of the Weight of a Grain ... If now for the more convenient Calculation, this last Animalculum and a Grain of Sand be supposed to be of the same Figure ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly declare simplifying assumptions (weights, shapes, unit conversions, equivalences between grains/sands/animalcula) before arithmetic so the reader can follow or dispute the chain of reasoning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use proportional reasoning and the Rule of Three
rubrics_metrics.description: compute according to the Rule of Three ... Since 100 is to 314 as the Diameter RE to the ... we shall find, by the Rule of Three, that this Circumference includes 62,800 Feet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply standard proportional arithmetic (Rule of Three), geometric formulae, and known ratios (e.g., circumference = pi·diameter, inverse-square relations) to convert observations into large-scale numerical estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply known mathematical/physical laws (inverse-square for light)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Number of the Particles of Light in two equaly great, but unequally distant, Places from the Flame, are to each other in an inverted Ratio of the Squares of their Distances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rely on accepted mathematical/physical principles (here the inverse-square relation for radiant intensity) to relate particle counts at different distances and to scale local observations to larger volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer conservative (under-)estimates to avoid overclaiming
rubrics_metrics.description: That we may not therefore be deceiv'd in our Calculation, we shall make choice of a much smaller Sum than we need do, and therefore only retain the Number 10², that alone being the greatest quantity of Light Particles in the Space of one of the Animalcula, or the Line A a; and we will throw away the rest Bc, Cc, Dd, &c.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with quantities that explode numerically, deliberately choose smaller/simpler numbers or truncate contributions to produce conservative lower bounds, making conclusions harder to dispute on grounds of exaggeration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make results intelligible by comparison to familiar objects
rubrics_metrics.description: If now for the more convenient Calculation, this last Animalculum and a Grain of Sand be supposed to be of the same Figure ... a Grain of Sand is equal to 1000 Millions of these Animalcula ... 100 Grains of Sand are equal to an Inch in Length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate microscopic magnitudes into comparisons with grains of sand, inches, drops, or known weights to give the reader intuitive sense of scale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use multiple converging lines of argument (experiments, geometry, thought experiments)
rubrics_metrics.description: I have been willing to prove here by degrees ... and thereto the Reader will be pleased to judge from which follows ... Now Mr. Leuwenhoek ... If then we argue after this manner ... Now if we divide a Foot into ten Parts ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine empirical observation, stepwise numerical calculation, geometric reasoning, and analogical argument so that independent methods point toward the same conclusion, strengthening persuasion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose methods appropriate to the intended audience
rubrics_metrics.description: A Mathematician will wonder, perhaps, why I did not find the Area of the Magnitude of the Minimus ... They must be pleas'd to observe; Not That I have omitted these Methods ... but my chief End being to render my self intelligible even to the meanest Capacity, rather than to please the Learned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor simpler, more accessible methods over more advanced mathematical techniques when the goal is to persuade or instruct a broad readership; explicitly justify methodological choices in light of audience comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend applicability across related materials
rubrics_metrics.description: This last being now proved about Water, we may easily see that it is applicable to many other fluid Matters, especially to such as are wet, and which by sticking to solid Bodies do moisten the same; for which reason we need not omit the touching of Oil, Spirits and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After establishing a result for one substance, argue its applicability to other similar materials (fluids, vapours, solids) by pointing to common observable behaviors or mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use physical effects (penetration, heating, combustion) to infer particle properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Now how much more minute Parts, Fire consists of, than all these above-mentioned Fluids, may appear from hence, that Air, Water, Oyl, and the like, are found to consist of such gross Parts, that they cannot pass through the Pores of Glass ... whereas there are no Pores ... in any Bodies through which the Particles of Fire cannot penetrate; which appears by their rendering all Bodies either glowing ... or putting them into Fusion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infer relative fineness, mobility, or velocity of particles from macroscopic effects such as permeability, ability to cause fusion/evaporation, or difficulty of exhausting air pumps; use such phenomena as indirect evidence for particle size and velocity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be explicit about numerical scaling and unit conversions
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us suppose, that a Drop of Water be of the Weight of a Grain, which 480 go to an Ounce Troy-Weight ... Now if we divide a Foot into ten Parts, and call each of em an Inch, 1 Cubical Foot will contain 1000 Cubical Inches ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show step-by-step how units and scales are converted (grains to ounces, inches to feet, cubic measures) so that readers can follow the arithmetic that leads to enormous final numbers.
